source_records.title: Characterization of high-pressure, underexpanded hydrogen-jet flames
source_records.observed_public_scope: The article reports the high-pressure jet-flame campaign and a measured stagnation-chamber pressure/temperature blowdown history. The indexed record reports an initial storage pressure near 431 bar and an approximately 500–600 s two-tube blowdown.

source_records.title: SAND2024-14886 technical report excerpt describing the Schefer et al. (2007) setup
source_records.observed_public_scope: The report describes eight hydrogen tanks totaling about 4,938 L, with two tanks used for the blowdown and flame tests, a 0.508 cm exit diameter, and optical/radiometer measurements.

source_records.title: Fundamentals of Hydrogen Safety Engineering I, jet-fire chapter
source_records.observed_public_scope: The chapter summarizes the 2007 campaign as two 617 L storage tubes at approximately 41.3 MPa with a 5.08 mm nozzle and about 500–600 s blowdown through the experimental hydraulic system.

source_records.title: Experimental evaluation of barrier walls for risk reduction of unintended hydrogen releases
source_records.observed_public_scope: A related 2007 tie-back campaign reports a 26.1 cm by 15.3 cm stagnation chamber and an approximately 2–3 s pneumatic-valve opening time. The publication does not establish that these exact boundary values apply to the primary 617 L Schefer 2007 pressure-decay trace.

supports: The frozen well-mixed vessel model is missing documented apparatus boundary details needed to explain early transient pressure-shape error.
A future explicit valve-opening and distributed line-inventory model is a plausible development direction, subject to a new untouched validation campaign.
does_not_support: Changing restriction, vessel volume, or production parameters to improve the existing result.
Claiming line-transient validation without a rights-cleared common-clock trace and resolved boundary channels.

next_action: Seek a rights-cleared apparatus export containing valve state/opening, upstream line geometry or equivalent line volume, pressure and temperature channels on a common clock; freeze a new holdout before opening outcomes.
